THE PERSON BEHIND THE STUDIO

A practice shapedby curiosity.

I’m Ruixi Feng, also known as Steven. Steven Studio brings together my explorations in art and design: a place to follow an idea from a drawing into an object, a space, a performance or a digital experience.

From observation to making

Drawing gives me a way to look closely at structure, light and texture. Alongside portrait and still-life studies, I explore abstract digital images and light-painting photography. Working across these media has led me towards physical models and installations, where the qualities of acrylic, metal foil, fibre and light become part of the idea itself.

Questions that connect the work

My projects often return to the relationship between people and their surroundings. Frostfade, Color Sphere Marine Blossoms and ArgenRubi imagine plants adapting to a polluted future. Temporal Palimpsest and Temporal Dissolution consider the passage of time, memory and the pressure of contemporary life. These questions also extend into my spatial and urban concepts, furniture studies and interaction design.

Research, test, rethink

I develop ideas through observation, research, sketches and material experiments. In Sacred Celestial Illumination Chair, I explored how a chair model could shape light and shadow. In Tempus Forestum Retreat, I moved from everyday observations and user research into interface flows and scenario visualisations. Across these projects, I use making and testing to discover what an idea can become, then revise it as I learn.

Recognition along the way

In 2024, Frostfade, Color Sphere Marine Blossoms and ArgenRubi received the Gold, Silver and Bronze Medals respectively in the Global Art Creation Award, organised by the European Association of Culture and Education. I see this recognition as encouragement to keep experimenting, while allowing my practice to remain open and evolving.
